prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Labour’s 2010 Manifesto sets out a programme for a future fair for all, rejecting “business as usual” after the global financial crisis. It argues for active, reforming government that protects the recovery now, rebuilds the economy on fairer, stronger foundations, renews public services with people in control, strengthens communities through rights and responsibilities, and restores trust in politics with transparency and democratic reform. The watchwords are fairness, responsibility and long-termism: protect frontline services, make those with the broadest shoulders pay more, demand responsibility from all, and invest to create jobs and green growth.

Economy and jobs: Labour will secure the recovery by avoiding immediate cuts, then more than halve the deficit by 2014 through growth, fair tax rises (bank bonus tax, reduced pension relief for the best-off, 50p rate over £150k, 1p NI with protections for low earners), and cuts to lower-priority spending, pay restraint and efficiency. It will reform finance (tougher capital, living wills, global levy, action on pay), diversify industry, and back enterprise: UK Finance for Growth (£4bn), a Green Investment Bank, high-speed rail, universal broadband, stronger science, modern industrial strategy and export support. One million skilled jobs, expanded apprenticeships, SME finance adjudication and simpler regulation will underpin full employment and rising living standards. Work will always pay (minimum wage rising with earnings; a £40 Better Off in Work guarantee), with job guarantees to end long-term unemployment and tough-but-fair welfare reform.

Public services: Frontline spending on childcare, schools, NHS and policing is protected. Reform puts citizens in control: guarantees on school standards and 3Rs catch-up, takeovers of persistently weak schools, more academies and federations, personal tutors and broader curricula; in the NHS, legally binding rights (18-week treatment or funded private care; one-week cancer test results; over-40s health checks), more choice, prevention and care at home, access to talking therapies, and empowered staff and mutuals. A new National Care Service will provide free home care for those with the greatest needs now, cap residential care costs after two years, and move to comprehensive, free-at-point-of-use adult care after 2015.

Communities, safety and migration: Police and PCSO numbers are maintained; neighbourhood teams spend 80% of time on the beat, failing forces can be taken over, and early intervention targets 50,000 troubled families. Fast, effective action on anti-social behaviour is guaranteed, with community payback expanded. Technology like CCTV and DNA (with safeguards) will help cut crime. Immigration is controlled through a points-based system (no unskilled non‑EU migration), stronger English and integration requirements, and a clear link between citizenship and responsibilities.

Family, culture and environment: More flexible parental leave (a new Fathers’ Month), a Toddler Tax Credit, flexible working for older workers and ending default retirement at 65; pensions re‑linked to earnings from 2012 and new Personal Pension Accounts. Labour protects the BBC, free museums, and community institutions like post offices and pubs, and leverages the 2012 Olympics for a golden decade of sport. A green industrial revolution will deliver around 40% low‑carbon electricity by 2020 and 400,000 green jobs, with home insulation on “pay as you save,” smart meters, zero waste, greener transport, protected Green Belt, more woodland, and a Supermarkets Ombudsman.

New politics and Britain in the world: Labour will hold referenda on AV and a democratic, accountable Second Chamber, legislate for fixed-term Parliaments, create a lobbyists register and recall, open up government data, and strengthen local democratic scrutiny. Internationally, it supports troops and veterans, a Strategic Defence Review while retaining the nuclear deterrent, a leading role in the EU, a rules‑based global order, and development leadership with 0.7% aid from 2013 to meet the Millennium Development Goals.
